title: sdk-lifecycle-mini-roadmap-and-smoke-tests-notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact working doc to align on a minimal SDK lifecycle roadmap for the next two quarters plus a small, practical smoke-test matrix and developer checklist that can be shipped with the SDK starter bundles. Aim: reduce first-time-integration time and escape common early adopter failure modes without adding heavy process overhead.

Scope:
- SDKs: JS (browser + node), Python (sync/async), and a minimal Go client.
- Focus on developer experience (DX) for first 30 minutes: auth, quick request, streaming, error handling, telemetry opt-in, offline dev mode.
- Delivery: lightweight starter repo, a single-page quickstart, three smoke tests runnable in CI, and a minimal telemetry contract.

North-star success metrics (90 days post-rollout):
- Time-to-first-successful-call median <= 10 minutes for new signups using quickstart
- 80% of SDK onboarding support threads resolved by pointing to the starter-runbook
- CI smoke test pass rate >= 95% across internal apps integrating SDKs

Milestones (high-level):
1) Week 0–2: Starter repo skeleton + single-page quickstart (no streaming initially).
2) Week 3–5: Add streaming example, error patterns, minimal e2e smoke tests, and CI script.
3) Week 6–9: Telemetry events contract + opt-in UX; local-mode emulator (lightweight).
4) Week 10–12: Polish docs, sample apps, publish packages, and run internal adoption pods.

Minimum Acceptable Deliverables (MVP):
- single-file quickstart (index.js / quickstart.py) demonstrating: auth, simple text generation, streaming, and basic error handling.
- smoke-tests/ci: three tests (auth, simple gen, stream-to-completion) that run in <30s each in hermetic CI.
- telemetry-contract.md: list of telemetry events (names, shapes, privacy notes) + opt-out instructions.
- troubleshooting-runbook: top 8 common errors and fixes (auth, rate limits, bad model id, streaming hang, long prompt truncation).

Smoke Test Matrix (suggested):
- test-01-auth-basic: assert 200 + token usage header with valid API key.
- test-02-generation-short: send 1-paragraph prompt, assert deterministic-ish shape (response non-empty, cost header present).
- test-03-stream-accumulate: open streaming endpoint, accumulate tokens up to termination signal, verify final message and order.
Notes: keep tests hermetic (use dedicated CI key with minimal quotas) and mark flaky external network dependent parts as optional.

Telemetry hooks (minimal contract):
- event: sdk.initialized {sdk_name, sdk_version, env}
- event: sdk.call.started {operation, model_id, routing_hint?} (no prompt text)
- event: sdk.call.completed {operation, latency_ms, token_count, success:true/false}
- event: sdk.error {error_class, error_msg_summary} (truncate and hash any PII)
Privacy: All events must avoid sending prompt text; if a prompt fingerprint is needed, send a deterministic hash and store mapping only if customer opted into extended diagnostics. Opt-in default: false for user-level prompt telemetry.

Known Pitfalls & Proposed Mitigations (practical):
- Pitfall: Developers confuse API key scopes (hosted vs dedicated).
  - Mitigation: quickstart prints clear error with link to FAQ; add guard that detects credential type mismatch and suggests the right env var.
- Pitfall: Streaming appears stuck when network proxies buffer SSE/WS frames.
  - Mitigation: add explicit heartbeat frames in stream protocol and a client-side timeout with reconnection example.
- Pitfall: Long prompts truncated silently -> user surprised at output mismatch.
  - Mitigation: SDK warns when prompt length > model max tokens; expose helper to compute token usage locally.
- Pitfall: CI smoke tests flaky due to rate limits or ephemeral infra.
  - Mitigation: dedicated CI key + local mock server fallback; tests mark external network optional.

Developer checklist (to include in starter repo readme):
- [ ] install package (npm/pip/go get)
- [ ] set REDWOOD_API_KEY or use local mock credentials
- [ ] run quickstart: node quickstart.js or python quickstart.py
- [ ] run smoke tests: ./smoke/run.sh (CI-friendly)
- [ ] enable telemetry (optional) and run a couple of instrumented calls
- [ ] read troubleshooting-runbook for next steps

Example error messages to surface (short strings to copy into SDK):
- "Invalid API key scope: found 'dedicated' but expected 'hosted'. See: <link>"
- "Streaming appears paused — check proxy buffering or enable heartbeat mode."
- "Prompt length exceeds model capacity (approx X tokens). Trim or use chunking helper."

Developer support flow (first 30 days):
- Tier 0: quickstart + README + runbook + smoke-tests -> aim to resolve 60% of incoming onboarding tickets.
- Tier 1: template reproduction repo (paired debugging) -> for the next 30%.
- Escalation to eng-developer-experience for systemic regressions or flaky tests.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we ship streaming in week 2 or wait until telemetry contract is in place? (Tradeoff: earlier DX vs. more surface area to instrument.)
- Which hash algorithm for prompt fingerprinting if users opt-in? (SHA-256 recommended; confirm legal review.)
- Do we include a local-mode binary (small Go mock) or keep the mock in node/python only?

Next steps (action items):
- Marcus: scaffold starter repo + CI skeleton (due 2025-11-10)
- Lina: draft telemetry_contract.md and privacy blurb (due 2025-11-12)
- Diego: create smoke-tests harness and CI key (due 2025-11-14)
- Aisha: assemble troubleshooting-runbook and publish single-page quickstart (due 2025-11-18)

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Keep the starter code as copy-paste friendly — a single file that "just works" is more valuable than a multi-file example that requires env juggling.
- Prefer explicit, actionable error messages. When we add links, point to single canonical troubleshooting doc rather than many micro-articles.
- Consider a tiny CLI: `rw-sdkrun quickstart` that bootstraps env and runs the smoke tests in one command for internal demos.

End of working draft.
(Will iterate after initial internal pod run and 2–3 early adopter integrations.)
